name: Zhēng Shàngyóu
description: Zhēng Shàngyóu ('Struggling Upstream' / 'Climb to the Top') is a Chinese shedding/climbing game similar to President. 54-card deck (52 + 2 jokers). Play ascending combinations (singles/pairs/triples/sequences/bombs). First out wins. Ranking: 3-A-2-BlackJoker-RedJoker. Bombs beat any combination.

content.text: Zhēng Shàngyóu ('Struggling Upstream' / 'Climb to the Top') is a Chinese shedding/climbing game similar to President. 54-card deck (52 + 2 jokers). Play ascending combinations (singles/pairs/triples/sequences/bombs). First out wins. Ranking: 3-A-2-BlackJoker-RedJoker. Bombs beat any combination.

Zhēng Shàngyóu (争上游), meaning 'Struggling Upstream', is a Chinese climbing card game whose name is said to recall a literary image of a fish swimming against the current in early spring; some associate it with the Cultural Revolution era. The game exists in several variations and is closely related to Japanese Dai Hin Min, Vietnamese Tien Len, Chinese Big Two, and Western President. It was brought to the UK in 1979 by John McLeod, who learned it from interpreter Zhang Chuansheng during a British Go players' visit to China; in Britain it became known as Pits, referring to the predicament of the losing players. It is particularly popular in Shanghai, Zhejiang, and Jiangsu and forms the basis for many modern climbing games.
Three to five players (four or more in some descriptions; best with 4–6).
54 cards: standard 52 plus two distinguishable jokers (Red and Black). Rank order 3 low to A, then 2, Black Joker, Red Joker.
Dealt singly anticlockwise from dealer until pack is exhausted; depending on player count some players may have one more card.

items.text: Twos in sequences: Some allow twos as natural cards in single sequences (e.g. K-A-2 in one suit beats Q-K-A).
Partnership (4 players): Four players in two teams, partners opposite; rules and scoring as individual but partners combine scores.
